correctness.rationale: The proof handles n<=k via degree n-1, n>k with blanks on both sides via surjectivity and forced equal supports, and one fully colored side via singleton-color count q >= 2k-n and forced opposite sites. All equality cases and boundaries n=k, n=2k are covered. For the matched supports, both sides carry one of each color. One-side-full assignments have exactly s singleton colors and k-s doubles, yielding the multinomial term. The provided standalone checker enumerates every labelled assignment at all weights up to the claimed minimum for 11 finite (n,k) test pairs; no lighter or unclassified examples occurred. Independently, the all-graph proof establishes the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The central new invariant is the exact number and classification of minimum singleton-rainbow service configurations on crown graphs for arbitrary n,k, including the matched-index restriction and one-side-full boundary, rather than a scalar inequality. Lange studies regular graph bounds and different families; Rao et al. give dual-server values under other operations; the closest accessible published two-rainbow multipartite enumerator permits doubleton labels and concerns complete multipartite hosts. Crown graphs are tensor products K_n x K_2, not included in those stated classes. Search did not identify a formula or stronger theorem implying the enumerator. Historical priority remains qualified by inaccessible foundational dual-server text.
residual_risks: The full foundational dual-server paper by Chellali, Haynes and Hedetniemi was not read; it may include narrower crown examples not advertised in abstract.
Earlier studies may use terms bipartite double cover, tensor product, dual-server or 2-rainbow domination; the searches are not proof of global priority.
The 2022 paper on generalized Petersen graphs contains a lift inequality; its full text was not read, but a scalar lift inequality alone cannot count all optimal crown assignments.

value.rationale: Complete enumeration and structural classification of minimum singleton service deployments on crown graphs is a natural missing invariant not recoverable from the minimum weight. The equality-type transition at n=2k and exact factor binomial(n,k) loss of optimum configurations after removing a perfect matching from a dense biclique quantify robustness of optimal allocations. The result is an infinite two-parameter statement and not a rephrasing of a general lower bound or a finite tabulation.
